title: Development of a Digitally Supported Care Network to Promote Medication Adherence and Self-Management Skills in People with Heart Failure
summary:
The aim of this study is to improve the care of patients with chronic heart failure. The study involves two main components:
Adaptation and optimisation of a digital health platform (CHES), which enables patients to independently record and transmit information about their health status to cardiology specialists.
Evaluation of a smart medication dispenser, designed to support patients in organising and adhering to their medication regimen.
In addition, a digital library embedded within the health portal provides patients with comprehensive information about their condition, empowering them through education and supporting self-management of heart failure.
The portal also offers extensive communication features. The heart failure care team provides not only training in the use of the digital health portal and smart medication dispenser, but also regular contact options for discussing condition-specific issues. Communication can take place via telephone, chat, or video consultations within the portal.
As part of the close follow-up of the patients, tailored education about the disease is also provided in order to enhance the affected individuals’ knowledge of their condition.
User feedback is collected at several points during the study to allow continuous refinement of the care components. The goal is to develop a modular, target group-oriented care model that can be transferred into standard care for people living with chronic heart failure.

The study aims to answer the following key questions:
1. What structural characteristics are required for a comprehensive care model to support long-term management of heart failure, and which barriers must be addressed to sustainably improve medication adherence and self-management?
2. How do medication and telemonitoring adherence, self-care and health literacy, medication knowledge, quality of life, usability of the technologies, and heart failure-specific physical and mental health change throughout the study?
3. How do patients with heart failure evaluate the digitally supported care model in terms of everyday usability, user-friendliness, and its impact on disease management?
4. What factors must be considered for the sustainable integration of the care model into routine healthcare from an economic, structural, political, clinical-practical, and scientific perspective?

Patients with chronic heart failure are at the centre of this study. We are seeking feedback on the digital patient portal, the smart medication dispenser, and the associated training and care components to enable a continuous user-centred development and adaptation of the intervention.
Participants will receive access for six months to a password-protected version of the digital health portal CHES, developed by Evaluation System Development Germany GmbH. The portal can be accessed via smartphone or PC, and a loan tablet can be provided if necessary.
They will also receive a smart medication dispenser (ANABOX®smart, developed by wirewire GmbH) to support daily medication management.

Participants are expected to enter the following health data into the portal daily:
Blood pressure, Heart rate, Body weight, Subjective well-being.

Additionally, at three defined time points during the six-month study, participants will be asked to complete several questionnaires within the portal. These cover: Usability of the technologies, Quality of life, Self-care and health literacy, Medication adherence

Prior to this, patients receive training on the appropriate use of the health portal and the medication dispenser, as well as on knowledge about their condition.
Throughout the six-month study period, participants will receive close support from a specialised heart failure care team, consisting of both nursing and medical professionals.
The daily input data will be reviewed by the care team to monitor for any deviations and to initiate appropriate adjustments to heart failure therapy if necessary.
Participants can contact nursing specialists via telephone and/or chat within the portal for condition-related concerns. In addition, video consultations are available.
Nursing staff will proactively contact participants at regular intervals (maximum once per week, minimum once per month) to address condition-related questions and to define and monitor individual therapy goals.
At the beginning (t0) and end (t2) of the study, participants will undergo a comprehensive heart failure-specific medical examination by study physicians, including: Physical examination (blood pressure, pulse, body weight), NYHA classification, Detailed medication and hospitalisation history, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), Blood sampling for heart failure-related parameters, Six-minute walk test
A separate session will also be held with the nursing team, in which individual care goals (e.g. fluid intake adjustments) will be discussed, agreed upon, and subsequently reviewed for effectiveness.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Chronic heart failure (ICD-10: I50, NYHA class II–III) as a primary or secondary diagnosis
- Treatment approach: conservative, pharmacological heart failure therapy
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
- Age <18 years
- Pregnancy
- Participation in other clinical trials
- Existing enrolment in a cardiology-based telemedicine programme
- End-stage heart failure, including ventricular assist device (VAD), heart transplantation and/or therapeutic limitations
- Life expectancy <1 year (cardiac or non-cardiac causes)
- Acute coronary syndrome/myocardial infarction within the past 12 months
- End-stage renal disease (on dialysis, or GFR <15 ml/min)
- Impaired or absent treatment adherence (e.g. due to dementia, alcohol or drug abuse)
- Limitations in access, use, or handling of the telemonitoring platform (e.g. intellectual disability, paralysis, blindness, dementia)
- Congenital heart defects (Grown-Up Congenital Heart Disease – GUCH)
- Specific cardiomyopathies (e.g. hypertrophic [HOCM], arrhythmogenic right ventricular [ARVC], restrictive [RCMP], peripartum cardiomyopathy [PPCM])
- Acute or active myocarditis (<12 months)
- Liver cirrhosis (hepatorenal syndrome, Child-Pugh class B or C)
